layout_dets.text: Abstract—The passive films formed on Fe-19Cr-9Ni in solutions of 0.3 M NaCl (pH 5.4) and 0.3 M NaCl

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (pH 9.0) have been characterized by variable angle XPS. Additional studies were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conducted to determine the effect of the pH change on the passive film and which agent was responsible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the deprotonation found in the film produced in the molybdate solution. It is proposed that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: anions reinforce the action of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in enhancing the bipolarity of the film and thereby significantly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: region, forming a more protective

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: barrier layer.

layout_dets.text: INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FoR MANY years, it has been known that molybdates may act as corrosion inhibitors,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increasing, for example, the resistance of stainless steels to localized corrosion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The object of this paper is to further evaluate the model previously proposed for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the role of Mo in the corrosion resistance of Mo bearing alloys, by comparing it with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the passivating behavior of aqueous molybdates, thereby developing a comprehen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sive understanding for the action of Mo as both an alloying agent and a corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inhibitor. For this study, variable angle XPS was used to analyse the composition of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the passive films formed on Fe-19Cr-9Ni stainless steel at -0.180 V(SCE) in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: de-aerated NaCl solutions. The primary film studied was the one resulting when the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: film formed in 0.3 M NaCl after passivation for 60 min is subjected to an additional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 15 min of passivation following the addition of molybdate. Since the addition of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the NaCl solution causes a pH change from 5.4 to 9.0, a second study

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was performed which repeated the experiment using a 0.3 M NaCl solution adjusted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to pH 9.0 with NaOH in order to determine the effect of the increase in pH on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nature of the passive film. Comparison of the films formed in 0.3 M NaCl solution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (pH 5.4) for 60 and 75 min were also made. Since the partial reduction of molybdate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to hydrated Mo dioxide was observed, further work was performed to determine

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which Mo species was responsible for the deprotonation.

layout_dets.text: EXPERIMENTAL METHOD

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The composition of Fe-19Cr-9Ni stainless steel (SS) investigated in this paper is given in Table 1. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: samples

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were sealed in a pre-evacuated quartz tube and annealed at 1100+C for 3 h

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: followed by a water quench, carried out by breaking the quartz tube under water. Since previous work1º

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by this group found that electropolishing could cause surface artifacts due to anodic segregation, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: samples were mechanically polished up the grades from 600 grit to a 0.25 μm diamond polish finish.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Polarization was performed in a conventional Greene cell which was de-aerated by purging with argon

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for 2 h. All potentials were measured against a saturated calomel electrode (SCE). Specimens were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cathodically polarized at —1.150 V(SCE) for 15 min to reduce the polish-formed film. The specimens were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: then either potentiodynamically polarized in the anodic direction at 1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to obtain the polarization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: curves or were pulsed to —0.180 V(SCE) and maintained there for a specified period of time in order to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grow the passive films to be studied by XPS. The entire procedure was executed in an argon-purged glove

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: box. It has been previously shown that the transfer of freshly passivated stainless steel through the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: atmosphere can lead to a minor structural modification of the iron component of the passive film."

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Following the passivation treatment, the specimens were removed from the cell, washed with de-aerated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: doubly distilled water, dried in argon, and mounted onto the XPS holder. The samples were then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transferred under argon from the glove box to the spectrometer. Each of the XPS analyses were performed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on separate freshly prepared samples.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The solutions used in this study were 0.3 M NaCl (pH 5.4), 0.3 M NaCl + 0.16 M

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 0.3 M NaCl (pH 9 adjusted by adding 0.1 M NaOH). The solution used for the cathodic branch of all

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the polarization curves was 0.3 M NaCl (pH 5.4). At the open circuit potential, the solution was adjusted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with NaOH or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the appropriate concentration for passivation. This was done to protect against

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the possible reduction of molybdate during cathodic polarization. The two doped films were grown for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 60 min in 0.3 M NaCl at –180 mV; then the solution was adjusted to the pertinent composition and a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: further 15 min of passivation was carried out. No notable change in current density was observed during

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the adjustment of the solutions, indicating that the procedure did not unduly disrupt the previously formed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: film.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The decision to apply the molybdate solution after the formation of the passive film in the 0.3 M NaCl

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (pH 5.4) solution was made to insure that the molybdate resided in the outer region of the film as was found

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in our previous work.7 Thus it was possible to compare the effect on passivity of the aqueous molybdate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the Mo alloy addition.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All XPS measurements were performed with a V.G. Scientific ESCA 3 MK II controlled by a V.G.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1000 data system. A Mg

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1253.6 eV) source was used for XPS and operated at 200 W. The base

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pressure was 1 to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: torr. All XPS measurements were carried out at high and low take-off angles

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (50° and 20°, measured with respect to the plane of the sample) to observe the inner and outer layers of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: films, respectively.12 For reference the binding energy of the Au 4f 7/2 line was taken as 83.8 eV and was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found to have a FWHM of 1.4 eV under the experimental conditions. The XPS spectra were corrected for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: charge shifting by taking the carbon 1s spectrum from the adventitious carbon as 284.6 eV. The entrance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and exit slit widths of the hemispherical analyser were 4 mm. According to Seah,13 this would make the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: half angle of the spectrometer for photo-electron emission 0.095 radians.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All data were smoothed utilizing a 15 point quadratic/cubic least squares program following the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method developed by Savitsky and Golay,14 which has been modified to cover the truncation errors at the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: end of the spectra. Since the Cr 2p peak produces a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: satellite on the high binding energy side of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cr 2p peak, a satellite subtraction program dependent on the pass energy of the analyser was used to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eliminate the satellite.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The background caused by the rising tail on the high binding energy side of the spectra was simulated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using the curve fitting parameters. The two background parameters of the synthesis program, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provide a straight background with a specifiable slope, would be primarily set to the background of the low

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: energy side of the spectra with some consideration to the high energy side for slight adjustments. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resulting difference would then be handled by adjusting the intensities of the standardized peaks to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compensate for the rising high energy tails. This would prove consistent within an elemental series since

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the same background procedure would have been used in developing the parameters for the standards.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The curve-fitting program allowed the operator to synthesize peaks by specifying the peak's position,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: height, width and shape. The optional shape parameters included the peak's Gaussian/Lorentzian ratio

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and tail characteristics which are height, slope and exponential to linear tail mix.1⁵As stated above, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: program also included y-axis intercept and background slope parameters bringing the total of fitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters used to nine. The parameters used came from the group's work on standards supplemented by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: those given in the literature. In general, our instrumentation gave FWHM 10–25% narrower than those

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: given in Allen et al.16

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To aid in the correct fitting of the peaks, the simpler peaks such as oxygen were fitted first to provide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information as to how the more complex peaks should be fitted. Since curve fitting can provide several

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions to the same spectrum, spectral resolution was enhanced by applying variable angle XPS in order

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to determine the best fit. As an additional precaution against spurious fittings, restrictions were placed on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: manipulating the remaining fitting parameters. The peak position was allowed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: margin, since

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from our standards work this was the uncertainty in values obtained. The FWHM also was considered to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , and a correction of 0.3 eV was made if the standard was taken with Al

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: radiation instead of Mg

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: radiation. While our software provides no specific statistical tests for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: peaks have failed to show a correspondence indicating any dependence of one peak on another due to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: possible satellite or energy loss phenomena.

layout_dets.text: DISCUSSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This study is concerned with the changes caused to passive films already formed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in 0.3 M NaCl (pH 5.4) by additional 15 min passivations in different solutions. To

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ensure that this additional 15 min of passivation required for the studies did not result

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in any significant aging phenomena, two films formed in the 0.3 M NaCl (pH 5.4)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution for different passivation times were investigated. The differing times were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 60 and 75 min. By comparing the Cr and O spectra from the 60 min film in Fig. 2 to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the spectra of the 75 min film in Figs 3 and 4, one sees that there are no significant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differences between the films formed by passivating for 60 or for 75 min in 0.3 M NaCl

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: One should explore three questions to determine whether the changes brought

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: about in the films by additional 15 min passivations in different solutions were due to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the presence of molybdate, a reduced Mo species or to the pH of the molybdate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution. First, are the films produced in the 0.3 M NaCl (pH 9.0) solution and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: molybdate (pH 9.0) the same? If so, then the resulting films are probably the product

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the pH change. Secondly, if the films are not the same, what species from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: molybdate solution is responsible for the difference? Thirdly, if the film produced in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the molybdate solution is not the product of the pH change and a Mo species is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: responsible for the difference, what mechanism is forming the film? In the following

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
